answer: Identity mirror escrow. Each new identity must post a deposit that is refunded only after it completes K interactions with distinct existing identities, each of which must co-sign a sonnet of its own prior activity history. The escrow is slashed to the counterparties if any co-signer is later shown to be a clone, so a sybil cluster must fund real deposits across all its members and expose them to correlated loss. The kernel rule: payouts route through the oldest identity in each interaction graph, making clone farms pay a persistent rent to genuine nodes.
